candidates.after: Have to plus base verb; has to with he, she or it. Do not have to means that an action is unnecessary, whereas must not expresses prohibition.
candidates.before: have to + base verb; don't have to means no necessity, not prohibition. The negative source group is treated as a polarity pattern, not automatically a new Sense.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Use billion without plural -s after an exact number: two billion dollars. Use billions of for an unspecified very large quantity.
candidates.before: Source NUMBER has no direct Master POS enum; OTHER is a local review proposal, not an approved noun conversion. Use billion after exact numbers without plural s.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Countable; a book about a subject, borrow a book from a library. Book can name a printed volume or an electronic work.
candidates.before: Countable; do not infer identity with an existing booking Sense from the same spelling.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Before a noun or after a linking verb: a big suitcase; the suitcase is too big. Bigger and biggest are the comparative and superlative forms.
candidates.before: Physical size in this example; not the importance proposal.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Countable: two blocks from a place; walk three blocks. Block lengths vary between streets and cities.
candidates.before: Two blocks from a place describes street distance, not the enclosed area of a city block. Block lengths vary; owner may later propose a separate area Sense if supported. This overlay creates no new Sense.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Transitive: block a road, path or entrance. Blocked and blocking are the regular forms.
candidates.before: block + route or entrance; no street-section identity implied.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Transitive: book a ticket, room or table; book something for a date or for a number of people.
candidates.before: book + ticket, room or table; compare with existing booking evidence without reusing an ID.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Countable: a bowl of soup; pour soup into a bowl. Bowls is the plural form.
candidates.before: Countable dish; the sporting verb bowl is outside this evidence scope.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Often modifies an adjective or participle: broadly applicable, broadly supported. It can describe relevance or acceptance across many areas or people.
candidates.before: broadly applicable; collocation and boundary with generally need human review.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Informal countable noun: one buck, five bucks. The surrounding context identifies which dollar currency is meant.
candidates.before: Informal; specify currency context when necessary. Animal and verb uses are not in this proposal.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Countable: a cable connecting two devices; connect something with a cable. Cables is the plural form.
candidates.before: Countable; a rope-like load-bearing cable may need a separate sense review.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Usually uncountable: carbon dioxide; carbon dioxide emissions. Use a noun such as molecule when counting individual units.
candidates.before: Usually uncountable; chemical formula and scientific precision require subject review before publication.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: A noun phrase with cosmopolitan before city: a cosmopolitan city; several cosmopolitan cities.
candidates.before: A compositional noun phrase; owner must decide whether it needs a Lexeme or should be represented as a construction/example.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Countable: a greenhouse gas; greenhouse gases. Gas emissions names substances released into the air.
candidates.before: Scientific wording remains a subject-review requirement; do not infer exam suitability.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Countable: a light, several lights. Turn on, switch off or replace a light.
candidates.before: Countable device; existing Master noun meanings need comparison, not lemma-only reuse.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Transitive: light a candle. The past and past participle can be lit or lighted; lighting is the ing form.
candidates.before: light, lit or lighted; no procedural instruction for hazardous fire-setting.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Transitive: record an interview or meeting. The verb usually stresses the second syllable; the noun usually stresses the first.
candidates.before: Transitive; noun/verb stress differs and requires pronunciation review. Information capture subtypes may need later splitting.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Countable: keep a record of an event; records of repairs. Of introduces what the information concerns.
candidates.before: a record of + event; a physical audio disc is not proposed from this group alone.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Intransitive when describing a machine's operation: the generator runs. Run a program is a transitive construction.
candidates.before: Intransitive in this example; run a program is a related transitive use needing boundary review.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Transitive: run a business or organization. Ran is the past tense and run is the past participle.
candidates.before: run + organization; no identity equivalence with physical motion.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Usually uncountable: a glass of water; fill a glass with water.
candidates.before: Usually uncountable; runtime #11 remains distinct from the owner-excluded existing Master verb pair.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.

candidates.after: Transitive: water a plant or water the garden. Watered and watering are the regular forms.
candidates.before: Transitive; possible similarity to the existing Master verb is a review candidate, never approval to map runtime #11.
candidates.selectionBasis: Highest number of still-unreviewed proposals in one original batch (22); review one whole 20-group/37-Sense batch. Risky proposals are included for explicit disposition, not promised for application.
